title: Daily totals from frequency: BD, TDS, QDS and hourly intervals
blurb: Turn a dose and a frequency into a 24-hour total in mg, g or tablets without mixing up intervals and counts.
question: A woman is prescribed labetalol 400 mg every 8 hours. The tablets available contain labetalol 200 mg each. How many tablets will she take in 24 hours?

teach.body: Formal rule: total per 24 hours = single dose × number of administrations in 24 hours. For an hourly interval, doses per day = 24 ÷ interval. Plain English: work out one dose, count how many times it is given in a day, then multiply. Part A midwifery and adult papers ask for daily totals in mg, g or tablets.
teach.cite: FACTS.md section 4 (total per day), Pearson VUE NMC midwifery practice paper

head: Written as
Means
Doses / 24 h
teach.caption: Interval in hours is not the number of doses: divide 24 by it.

teach.h: Worked example: Grace on the antenatal ward
teach.body: Grace Adeyemi, 31, is prescribed labetalol 400 mg 8-hourly. Tablets are 200 mg. Tablets per dose = 400 ÷ 200 = 2. Doses per day = 24 ÷ 8 = 3. Tablets in 24 hours = 2 × 3 = 6. Total dose = 400 mg × 3 = 1200 mg. Sense-check: 6 tablets × 200 mg = 1200 mg ✓.

teach.caption: Three doses fit in 24 hours: the fourth time point belongs to the next day.

teach.text: Reading the interval as the count: "6-hourly" is 4 doses a day, not 6, and "4-hourly" is 6 doses, not 4. Always divide 24 by the interval.

teach.body: Read the last sentence of the stem twice. "How many tablets should be given?" means one dose. "How many tablets in 24 hours?" or "total daily dose" means multiply. If the answer is asked in g and the dose is in mg, divide by 1000 at the end.

items: Total per day = single dose × doses per day.
Doses per day = 24 ÷ interval in hours.
Classic error: treating the interval number as the dose count.
Check whether the stem asks for one dose or a daily total, and in which unit.

summary: You can now convert BD, TDS, QDS and hourly intervals into doses per day and calculate daily totals in mg, g or tablets. You can also avoid confusing an interval in hours with the number of doses.

A.q: A person is prescribed 500 mg of a medicine four times a day. What is the total dose in 24 hours?
A.why: Four times a day = 4 doses. Total = 500 mg × 4 = 2000 mg.

whyNot.0: Used three doses (TDS) instead of four.
whyNot.2: This is one dose, not the 24-hour total.

A.q: A patient is prescribed 1 g of a medicine every 6 hours. What is the total dose in 24 hours? Please use the correct unit.
A.why: Doses per day = 24 ÷ 6 = 4. Total = 1 g × 4 = 4 g.

whyNot.1: This is a single dose, not the daily total.

A.q: A woman is prescribed labetalol 400 mg three times a day. The tablets available contain labetalol 200 mg each. How many tablets will she take in 24 hours?
A.why: Tablets per dose = 400 ÷ 200 = 2. Three doses a day: 2 × 3 = 6 tablets.

whyNot.1: This is the number of tablets in one dose.
whyNot.2: This is the number of doses, not tablets.
whyNot.3: Used four doses (QDS) instead of three.

B.q: A person is prescribed 250 mg of a medicine every 12 hours. What is the total dose in 24 hours?
B.why: Doses per day = 24 ÷ 12 = 2. Total = 250 mg × 2 = 500 mg.

B.q: A patient is prescribed 10 mg of a medicine every 4 hours. What is the total dose in 24 hours?
B.why: Doses per day = 24 ÷ 4 = 6. Total = 10 mg × 6 = 60 mg.

whyNot.2: Multiplied by 24 hours instead of the number of doses.

B.q: A person is prescribed 750 mg of a medicine twice a day. What is the total daily dose in grams? Please use the correct unit.

whyNot.0: Correct total in mg but not converted to grams.
whyNot.1: This is one dose in grams, not the daily total.
whyNot.2: Used four doses instead of two.

C.q: A woman is prescribed 500 mg of a medicine every 12 hours. The tablets available contain 250 mg each. How many tablets will she take in 24 hours?
C.why: Tablets per dose = 500 ÷ 250 = 2. Doses per day = 24 ÷ 12 = 2. Total = 2 × 2 = 4 tablets.

whyNot.0: This is one dose (2 tablets), not the 24-hour total.
whyNot.3: Used four doses a day instead of two.

C.q: A patient is prescribed 400 mg of a medicine every 8 hours for 2 days. The tablets available contain 200 mg each. How many tablets are needed for the 2 days?
C.why: Tablets per dose = 400 ÷ 200 = 2. Doses per day = 24 ÷ 8 = 3. Over 2 days: 2 × 3 × 2 = 12 tablets.

whyNot.0: This covers one day, not two.
whyNot.1: Took "every 8 hours" as eight doses a day.
whyNot.3: Used four doses for one day only.

C.q: A person is prescribed two 500 mg tablets of a medicine four times a day. What is the total dose in 24 hours?
C.why: One dose = 2 × 500 mg = 1000 mg. Four doses: 1000 × 4 = 4000 mg.

whyNot.1: Counted one tablet per dose instead of two.
whyNot.2: This is one dose, not the daily total.
whyNot.3: Used three doses instead of four.

reteach.title: Divide 24 by the interval
reteach.question: A medicine is given every 6 hours. How many doses is that in a day?

blocks.body: Every 6 hours means a dose at, for example, 0600, 1200, 1800 and 2400: four doses. The quick sum is 24 ÷ 6 = 4. The 6 is the gap, not the count.

blocks.text: Multiplying the dose by the interval ("6-hourly, so × 6") gives a total 50% too high.

explain.body: BD = twice a day, TDS = three times a day, QDS = four times a day. They tell you the count directly.

test.q: A person is prescribed 300 mg of a medicine TDS. What is the total dose in 24 hours?
test.why: TDS = three times a day. Total = 300 mg × 3 = 900 mg.

test.q: A patient is prescribed 50 mg of a medicine every 6 hours. What is the total dose in 24 hours?
test.why: Doses per day = 24 ÷ 6 = 4. Total = 50 mg × 4 = 200 mg.

explain.body: Find tablets per dose first (want ÷ have), then multiply by doses per day.

test.q: A person is prescribed 20 mg of a medicine QDS. The tablets available contain 10 mg each. How many tablets will be taken in 24 hours?
test.why: Tablets per dose = 20 ÷ 10 = 2. QDS = 4 doses. Total = 2 × 4 = 8 tablets.

whyNot.1: This is the number of doses, not tablets.
whyNot.3: Used three doses instead of four.

explain.h: mg to g at the end

test.q: A patient is prescribed 250 mg of a medicine every 6 hours. What is the total daily dose in grams? Please use the correct unit.

whyNot.2: This is a single dose in grams.
whyNot.3: Correct total in mg but not converted to grams.
